answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. Rewards are paid only after peers verify completed work, and proven fraud burns the lock; creating a thousand accounts therefore does not create free influence. An attacker must buy and immobilize substantial capital, then risks losing it. The river of ordinary tasks can still flow, while a summit of high-value jobs stays behind a ledge of higher stake requirements.
